findings.title: Provisioning can mark the tick cluster as provisioned even when setup fails
findings.description: `setup_backup` can fail to create the tick root, configure archiving, or install the new cron file while still returning success: `step_apply` allows every `MISSING` or `DRIFT` line beginning with `17/tick` via `APPLY_ALLOWED`’s `^MISSING 17/tick arm-file ` exception only for the arm file, but `setup_not_ok` tests allowed patterns with `re.search`, so `^PENDING RESTART 17/tick ` is intended only for pending restarts. More importantly, the broad `CHECK_ALLOWED` pattern `^(\S+|PENDING RESTART) 17/tick ` accepts any status token for any tick item in the precheck, including `DRIFT` and `MISSING`. This can let the cutover proceed despite pre-existing tick-related drift, rather than ensuring production is healthy and tick is not yet configured. Restrict the check allowance to the expected missing tick items and explicit pending-restart state.

findings.title: Health and push jobs are treated as successful regardless of their exit status
findings.description: `run_health` discards the `CompletedProcess` returned by `shell`, and `step_offsite` likewise ignores the push command’s exit status. A failed command can therefore be followed by a stale prior `FLAGS` line or a successful `rclone check`, allowing these verification steps to pass without the requested job having completed successfully. Check and record each command’s return code before accepting its log output or continuing the offsite comparison.

findings.title: Cutover report can be lost on unexpected step errors
findings.description: `run_steps` catches only `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`; filesystem errors (for example, a missing health log at line 210 or a failed `read_text()` in `run_health`) and other unexpected exceptions escape before `main()` writes the report. This contradicts the script’s documented guarantee that the report is still written on failure. Handle unexpected errors at the process boundary, recording the failure and writing the report, while retaining the exception details.

findings.title: Rehearse mode creates its target directory before check mode
findings.description: `mkdir -p "$REHEARSE"` runs before the check/apply steps, including when `--check` is set. Thus check mode, which is documented as changing nothing, creates a directory and can fail on an otherwise read-only audit due to permissions. Avoid that mutation in check mode and ensure rehearsal checks can render without creating the rehearsal root.

findings.title: Python project tooling does not type-check the new scripts or tests
findings.description: The configured mypy scope is only `src/manta_trading`; the new cutover scripts and their tests are outside it, and there is no strict `pyright` configuration. The new host-oriented script code is consequently not covered by the project’s static-analysis gate. Extend the checker configuration to include these files and tests, consistent with the Python rules requiring strict type checking of tests as well as implementation.

structured_findings.summary: Provisioning can mark the tick cluster as provisioned even when setup fails
Health and push jobs are treated as successful regardless of their exit status
Cutover report can be lost on unexpected step errors
Rehearse mode creates its target directory before check mode
Python project tooling does not type-check the new scripts or tests
